text.p: American prodigy Venus Williams has been waiting all week to make her first appearance at Wimbledon, but the rain has conspired against her.

The towering teenager with bead-bedecked hair and a ferocious serve, is one of 26 women whose scheduled first round matches have been postponed time after time as the rain has ruined the first week of the championships.
Only on Tuesday did organisers manage a full schedule and Thursday was a complete washout.

Referee Alan Mills said 96 matches had been completed so far and the tournament was some 120 behind schedule. Three men's first round matches were still unfinished going into Friday a day when players are usually embarking on their third-round contests.
Mills, who has still to decide whether to play on Sunday, the scheduled rest day, said Thursday had been "the wettest day I can remember."
The last time a complete day was lost to rain was in 1991 when no play was possible on the first Monday and only 52 matches had been completed by the end of the Thursday.
But this year's downpours have been heavier, sending disappointed fans scampering for cover with their soggy sandwiches.

A few gamely joined in the Centre Court sing-song organised by some energetic members of the armed forces, acting as stewards. Some managed a laugh when the soldiers put on a exhibition of cricket with an umbrella and tennis balls. But it was all pretty depressing.
Friday's forecast was no better with London's meteorological office predicting: "another wet and miserable day for most parts with further outbreaks of rain which could still be heavy at times."
They were hardly more optimistic for the weekend, though Monday is likely to be drier.
If the rain does let up on Friday Williams, who turned 17 last week, will make her long-awaited debut against Polish teenager Magdalena Grzybowska.

Stately Frenchwoman Mary Pierce, seeded nine, can finish her match, suspended after just one game in her favour, against Belgian Dominique van Roost and Mary Joe Fernandez the 11th seed can try to get through against Noelle van Lottum of France.

British fans are eager to see repeat success for Tim Henman, who plays Frenchman Jerome Golmard in the second round and Greg Rusedski, who ousted seventh seed Mark Philippoussis with a display of fearsome serving earlier in the week.
Rusedski, one of the biggest hitters on the tour meets another fast server, Jonathan Stark of the United States, in the second round.
Top seed Pete Sampras is due to play Germany's Hendrik Dreekman while his female counterpart Martina Hingis meets Olga Barabanshchikova of Belarus.
